title: US sanctions Chandigarh-based network accused of selling fake flags to Iran's tankers
dek: The US Treasury says an Indian couple's companies posed as ship registries for at least ten countries so that sanctioned tankers carrying Iranian oil could keep sailing. Eight Indian firms and four people are named.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The United States has imposed sanctions on a network based in Chandigarh that it accuses of selling false flags and fake certificates to tankers carrying Iranian oil. The US Treasury announced the action on Wednesday, 4 November, under "Operation Economic Outcast", its campaign against the money and shipping that keep Iran's oil trade going during the war.

Treasury named four people and nine linked companies, eight of them registered in India. It says the network posed as the official ship registries of countries that had never authorised it, which let sanctioned vessels appear to sail under a legitimate flag. Neither the people named nor the Indian government had responded publicly by Thursday morning IST.

## What happened

According to the Treasury release, the network is led by Suniel Kumar Sharma, who is based in India, and his wife, Jaspreet Preeti Shahid. Treasury says Shahid manages the couple's businesses on paper. Two Indian nationals, Ashwani Kumar Dhiman and Ishwinder Singh, were designated as nominal directors who act for the couple's company Aryavart Ship Management Private Limited.

The companies designated in India are Oceaniek Technologies India, Aryavart Ship Management, Precept Trends, Polynesia Maritime, Alexarya Finserv, Alexarya Media and Entertainment, Viharaboating, and the Aryavart Maritime and Educational Trust. The ninth is a Singapore company, Eswatini Maritime Affairs and International Ship Registry. Treasury says the businesses range from financial services to a media-streaming platform.

Sharma was designated for operating in Iran's petroleum sector under Executive Order 13902. The others were designated for helping him, or for acting for or being controlled by companies already listed. In the same action, Treasury also sanctioned Fugo Ground Services, a company in Turkey that it says handles ground services for six Iranian airlines placed under sanctions in September.

## How the scheme worked, according to Treasury

Every merchant ship must be registered with a country, its "flag state", which is responsible for checking that the ship is safe and insured. Treasury says the Sharma network bought web domains and built websites that offered ship registration, seafarer certificates and vessel classification in the name of countries that had not authorised it.

The release lists registries linked to the network that used the names of Dominica, Aruba, Guyana, Mali, Mozambique, Malawi, Sint Maarten, Timor-Leste, Nicaragua and Laos. It says the scheme goes back to at least 2014, when the couple allegedly tried to pose as Dominica's flag administration, and that Sharma shut some registries after they were reported in the press.

Treasury says Sharma set up the Eswatini registry in Singapore in 2023. Eswatini, a landlocked country in southern Africa, has publicly said the registry is not its own, but Treasury says it kept registering tankers carrying Iranian oil.

The release names four tankers it links to the network: Ping Shun, Lattafa, Binary Star and Vera. It says a fifth, Majestic X, was seized by US forces on 22 April 2026 while carrying Iranian oil under a false Guyana flag.

## Why false flags matter

Treasury says ships with false flags usually have no valid protection and indemnity insurance, the cover that pays for oil spills, wreck removal and crew injuries. After a serious accident, it warns, coastal countries could be left with "billions of dollars" in damage and nobody to pay.

Alongside the sanctions, Treasury's sanctions office (OFAC) issued an alert to the shipping industry. As reported by the shipping news site gCaptain, the alert lists warning signs such as unfamiliar flags, registration papers that cannot be checked, and a mismatch between a ship's claimed flag and the country code of its radio identity. OFAC said companies that serve falsely flagged ships could face penalties, and asked governments to report fake registries to the International Maritime Organization.

## Background

The US and Iran have been at war since earlier this year, and US forces are enforcing a maritime blockade of Iranian oil. Treasury began Operation Economic Outcast in August 2026 to target tankers, money-laundering networks and other ways Iran sells its oil, The Maritime Executive reported. Treasury says it is working with the European Union, the United Kingdom and Gulf partners.

Earlier US sanctions actions against Iran's oil trade have also named Indian companies and citizens, The Tribune has reported. India itself has a direct stake in keeping the Gulf shipping lanes open. An Indian seafarer was killed when an Indian-flagged vessel was attacked off Oman on 2 November, and an Iranian MP said this week that Indian ships were exempt from Iran's curbs in the Strait of Hormuz, though they would still have to pay transit fees.

## What they are saying

> "As we have said many times, under Operation Economic Outcast, you are either with us or against us." — US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent

Bessent added, according to gCaptain: "We know where you are, and we will sanction those who continue supporting the Iranian regime."

The Washington Times put the size of the action at 13 people and companies in the Sharma network; Treasury's own list names four people and nine linked companies. India's Ministry of External Affairs and the Directorate General of Shipping had not commented by the time of publication, and we could not reach the companies named.

## What happens next

Under US sanctions law, any property of the people and companies named that is in the US, or held by US persons, is frozen, and Americans are generally barred from dealing with them. Banks and firms outside the US that keep doing business with them risk being cut off from the US financial system themselves. For Indian banks, shipping agents and port operators, that makes the eight Indian companies difficult to deal with.

Watch for whether India's shipping regulator or investigating agencies act against the companies, and whether the countries whose names were used take the matter to the International Maritime Organization. A new round of indirect US-Iran talks through Qatari mediators is also under way; Treasury has said the sanctions campaign will continue while the war lasts.

## Key numbers

- 4 people and 9 linked companies designated in the Sharma network
- 8 of the companies are registered in India; 1 in Singapore
- At least 10 countries whose registries Treasury says were impersonated
- 2014: earliest attempt Treasury cites, involving Dominica
- 22 April 2026: Majestic X seized while flying a false Guyana flag
